152:/-! ## Interaction with the point projectors -/
154:/-- On a point of the line, Pauli line projectors of non-evaluating
155:polynomials vanish: every restricted low-degree encoding evaluates there.
156:Formalization-only auxiliary for items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
157:paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
174:/-- A Pauli line projector followed by a Pauli point projector at a point of
175:the line is the line projector when the line polynomial evaluates to the
176:point value, and zero otherwise. This is the exact consistency
177:`tau^{W,line}_{f''}` versus `tau^{W,u}_{f''(u)}` in items 2 and 3 of
178:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
179:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
216:/-- Pauli line and point projectors commute. -/
232:/-- Acting with a Pauli line projector on one half of the EPR state and a
233:Pauli point projector on the other half equals acting with their product on
234:the first half. Formalization-only support for the exact ancillary
235:consistency in items 2 and 3 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
236:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
255:/-- On an EPR pair, a point projector on the first factor and a line
256:projector on the second act as the product of the two projectors on the first
257:factor alone. This is the transport with the two factors interchanged, and it
258:uses the symmetry of the line projector rather than that of the point
259:projector. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary consistency of
260:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
261:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
280:/-- The EPR quadratic form of a line projector on one half and a point
281:projector on the other half is the EPR quadratic form of the line projector
282:alone when the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and zero
283:otherwise. This is the exact ancillary consistency in items 2 and 3 of
284:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
285:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:534-545`. -/
313:/-- The EPR overlap of a point projector on the first factor with a line
314:projector on the second vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates at the
315:point to the measured value, and otherwise equals the overlap of the line
316:projector alone. This is the interchanged form of
317:`stateQForm_eprState_tauLineProj_tauPointProj`, supporting
318:`def:expanded-line-measurement`, paper
319:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
347:/-! ## Perfect consistency on an EPR pair -/
349:/-- Acting with the same Pauli line projector on both halves of the EPR state
350:equals acting on one half. Symmetry transports the right action to the left,
351:where idempotence absorbs the repeated projector. This is the perfect
352:ancillary consistency used in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
353:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/
369:/-- The EPR quadratic forms of the Pauli line projectors on one half sum to
370:one. Formalization-only auxiliary for the ancillary overlaps in
371:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
372:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
407:/-- The diagonal overlap of the two Pauli line measurements on an EPR pair is
408:one. Thus the ancillary measurement contributes no consistency defect. This
409:is the perfect ancillary consistency in item 1 of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`,
410:paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`. -/

   910		two-variable polynomial error read in the corrected sum sense of
   911		\cite{gap:qpbt_pasting-product-error}, that is, a bound
   912		$C\bigl(\eps^{r} + (md/q)^{s}\bigr)$ with $C \ge 1$ and $r, s > 0$ on the
   913		closed nonnegative quadrant rather than the literal product form of the
   914		shorthand, such that the following holds. For
   915		$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ and every pair of
   916		lines $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$ there exists a POVM
   917		$\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$ acting on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$,
   918		with answers consisting of pairs of polynomials
   919		$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, such that on
   920		average over pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ independently sampled
   921		from the line-point distribution
   922		(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}),
   923		\[
   924			\big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}
   925			_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a,\ \mathrm{eval}_z(\cdot)=b]}
   926			\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   927			\simeq_{\delta_P}
   928			\big(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
   929		\]
   930		as well as all symmetric equivalents of this approximation. Moreover, if
   931		$\ell_W$ is axis-parallel, then $f_W \in \deg_{d}(\ell_W)$.
   932	\end{lemma}

   937			def:symmetric-equivalents, def:concrete-paired-line-measurement,
   938			lem:concrete-paired-line-degree-support}
   939		Define, for all lines $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ and
   940		$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the sandwich
   941		operator
   942		$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   943		= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}
   944		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}_{f_Z}
   945		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}$,
   946		which forms a valid POVM; since the lines measurements come from a valid
   947		strategy for the low-degree test, on an axis-parallel line $\ell_W$ the
   948		outcome $f_W$ lies in $\deg_d(\ell_W)$, and this property is inherited by
   949		$T$. As intermediate consistency relations, write
   950		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet} = \sum_b \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ and
   951		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b} = \sum_a \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ for the two
   952		marginals of the combined point measurement of
   953		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}. Applying
   954		Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} and then
   955		Lemma~\ref{lem:cool-closeness-fact} gives, on average over uniform
   956		$x, z$,
   957		$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   958		\approx_\delta
   959		\sum_b (\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   960		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$,
   961		and a direct norm computation from this display and
   962		\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} yields the marginal consistencies

   964		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$ and
   965		$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
   966		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$.
   967		From items 1 and 3 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}, converting
   968		between $\approx$ and $\simeq$ with Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} and

   972		distribution,

   974		(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}
   975		_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a]})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$
   976		together with the analogous relation for $Z$. The conclusion now follows
   977		from the pasting lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:pasting}) applied with
   978		$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ in the role of the combined measurement,
   979		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}$ and
   980		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}$ in the roles of the two factor
   981		measurements, $T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ in the role of the pasted measurement,
   982		$\delta := \delta_Q$, and $\eta := md/q$, the last justified by the
   983		Schwartz--Zippel bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree})
   984		applied to the polynomials $f_X, f_Z$ of total degree at most $md$; the
   985		two hypotheses of the pasting lemma are supplied by the preceding display

   987		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is that of two independent uniformly random lines. The
   988		register-exchanged comparison \eqref{eq:pasting-1-sym} is supplied by the
   989		symmetric equivalents of that preceding display, which
   990		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} establishes for all of its approximations.
   991		This gives the stated relation with $\delta_P$ equal to the pasting
   992		error, a $\poly(\eps, md/q)$ function, and the identical argument with
   993		the registers modified gives all symmetric equivalents.
   994	\end{proof}

6:# Self-consistency of the expanded line measurements
7:
8:This module proves item 1 of the expanded-line consistency lemma on the two
9:opposite-placement bipartitions. The strategy line measurements are
10:self-consistent between the two players on average over the line-point
11:distribution, because a disagreement on a sampled line is rejected by the
12:corresponding self-loop of the Pauli basis test; the Pauli line projectors are
13:perfectly consistent on an EPR pair; and the data-processing inequality
14:transfers the product estimate to the addition postprocessing that defines the
15:expanded line measurement.
16:
17:The module also records that the error parameter of a projective setting is
18:nonnegative, which is not assumed by the structure and is needed by the other
19:two items as well.
20:
21:## References
22:
23:The declarations formalize `enu:qld-comm-line-self-cons`, item 1 of
24:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, whose paper source is
25:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-532`.
26:-/

3:/-!
4:# Square-root error bounds for placed measurement families
5:
6:The consistency conclusions of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons` are stated with the
7:common error `deltaLine ε = √ε`, while the individual estimates of the proof
8:are linear in `ε` or already of square-root form. This module records the two
9:elementary facts that convert those estimates into the common form: the
10:state-dependent distance between two placed complete measurements never
11:exceeds `4`, and a quantity bounded by both `a * ε` and `4` is bounded by
12:`(a + 4) * √ε`.
13:
14:## References
15:
16:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
17:`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`.
18:-/
29:/-- The adjoint squares of a complete measurement sum to at most the identity.
30:This is the existing public measurement bound, used here for the uniform
31:distance estimate. -/
37:/-- A left-placed complete measurement is square-summable on the product
38:space, by the public measurement bound applied to its tensor placement. -/
47:/-- A right-placed complete measurement is square-summable on the product
48:space, by the public measurement bound applied to its tensor placement. -/
57:/-- The squared distance between two square-summable operator families is at
58:most four on a unit vector. Formalization-only auxiliary bounding the
59:state-dependent distance of `def:povm-distance` trivially. -/
93:/-- The state-dependent distance between two complete measurements placed on
94:opposite tensor factors is at most four. Formalization-only auxiliary: this is
95:the trivial bound used to pass from a linear error to the common square-root
96:error of `lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper
97:`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:527-545`. -/
121:/-- A nonnegative quantity bounded by a linear error `a * ε` with `1 ≤ a` and
122:by the trivial bound `4` is bounded by `(a + 4) * √ε`: for `ε ≤ 1` the linear
123:bound dominates, and for `ε ≥ 1` the trivial bound does. Formalization-only
124:auxiliary: this is the passage to the common square-root error of
125:`lem:qld-comm-line-cons`, paper

\section{At a glance}

\textbf{Difficulty.} The domain correction is elementary; the remaining
formal estimate requires the project's state-dependent Cauchy--Schwarz and
restricted-distribution arguments. \textbf{Estimated weight.} The correction
affects two Lean modules and their blueprint correspondence. It retains the
unfinished scalar estimate and isolates the existing pasting consistency
obligation. \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite sums, positivity, and real
square roots use Mathlib; the measurement construction and subline law use
the local quantum API. \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Completeness of a
POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
the proposed source proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
\begin{align*}
 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
\end{align*}
The paper's Claim 17-2 states
\[
 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.

\section{The construction used by the source}

The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
over the Z polynomial:
\[
 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the
claim and calculation at lines 1168--1201 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
labels \path{lem:qld-xz-lines} and \path{claim:17-2} in
\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The repair is tracked by \ghissue{414}; the earlier
proof attempt is \ghissue{405}.}

\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}

Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
players and every line pair, define a POVM by
\[
 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
\]
There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.

The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &=4.
\end{align*}
The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
polynomially small functions of $\eps$.

For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
\[
 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
 \qquad
 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
\]
The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

\section{Blueprint and formal comparison}

The concrete measurement domain is retained. The scalar obligation now
compares complex expectations with the complex modulus, preserving the
universal constant, factor $m$, and square-root error. It is named
\leanid{subline\_remove\_X\_factor\_direct}. Its distribution is still the
directly indexed law represented by \leanid{SubLineWitness}, not the
source law $D$. Thus it is a formalization-only obligation, linked from
\path{lem:claim-17-2-direct}, and is not a formalization of the source
claim. The source statement remains at \path{lem:claim-17-2}, with neither
a Lean link nor a completion mark.

The same scalar distinction affects Claim 17-1: an ordered product
$M^Z_bM^X_a$ need not be Hermitian, so a bound on the real part of its
correlation does not bound its complex modulus. The proved real-part
estimate is retained as
\leanid{subline\_replace\_by\_ordered\_product\_re\_direct}.
Its constant is $2\sqrt{\delta_Q}$: the squared-distance comparison on
one placement is $4\delta_Q$ and uses $W^\dagger W$, not $W^2$.
The source Claim 17-1 remains a separate uncertified blueprint statement.
Likewise \leanid{subline\_Z\_term\_near\_one\_re\_direct} retains the
proved real Z-overlap estimate with its directly indexed domain explicit.
No reality or distribution-transport theorem is asserted by these renamings.
The three existing source blueprint statements are reused; no duplicate
source theorem with a new proof hole is introduced.

The distribution discrepancy is documented in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}. Admissibility
does not supply the divisibility needed to instantiate the source line law
at dimension $2m+2$. The current correction neither adds that divisibility
as a hypothesis nor identifies the directly indexed law with the source law.
Scalar realignment is tracked in \ghissue{474} and review of PR~478.
The distribution and complex-overlap work under \ghissue{118} remains open;
its historical budget is unchanged.

The abstract combined-line witness record remains unchanged. Its fields
faithfully express the existential conclusion of the combined-lines lemma,
but do not characterize the construction used in its proof. The internal
consistency obligation now refers to the concrete sandwich. Both witness
existence proofs construct their records with that measurement. A later
argument needing the exact construction can use the consistency obligation
and the same explicit record; merely choosing an unspecified existential
witness does not recover its defining formula.\footnote{The Lean-only
obligation is \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines.lean}. Its hypotheses explicitly supply
a polynomially controlled point family. It retains the previously
unfinished consistency proof, to be discharged by the source's point-to-line
comparisons and pasting argument. The source-facing
\leanid{exists\_combinedLinesWitness} has an unchanged statement.}

There are two retained direct proof holes in the affected modules.
The first is \leanid{subline\_remove\_X\_factor\_direct}: apply complex
weighted Cauchy--Schwarz to bound $|A(T)-B(T)|$ by the square root of the
X-overlap deficit, then use the already proved
\leanid{exists\_concreteXPointOverlap\_deficit\_le}. That estimate already
uses \leanid{combinedLineMeasurement\_sum\_Z}, expanded line-point
consistency, and the separate X marginal of the directly indexed law.
Transport of this argument and of the real-part estimates to the source
law, including the complex estimate of Claim 17-1, is a separate remaining
obligation. No additional hole is introduced for that transport.

The second is \leanid{combined\_line\_measurement\_consistency}.
It must prove consistency of the same unconditioned X-Z-X measurement
with the supplied polynomially controlled joint point family on the
original product of line-point distributions, in every opposite placement.
The target and its discharge by the source point-to-line comparison and
pasting argument are described in
\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex}.
No marginal identity, deficit bound, or producer is added to a paper theorem.

\section{Conclusion}

The discrepancy lies in the formal quantification over arbitrary witnesses,
not in the paper's constructed-measurement assertion. The counterexample
forces a domain correction. Using the defined sandwich restores the measurement domain. The complex
scalar conclusion is restored for the directly indexed auxiliary obligation;
transport to the source distribution and the consistency construction remain
open. The source claims themselves retain their complex-modulus statements
without unsupported formalization marks.

\begin{definition}[Symmetric equivalents]
	\label{def:symmetric-equivalents}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Placement, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Placement.IsOpposite}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.place}
	\leanok
	\uses{def:expanded-state}
	For the remainder of this chapter, as well as in
	Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}, the
	six registers
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$
	are partitioned into two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first
	scheme takes $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ as one party and
	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ as the other; the second scheme takes
	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ as the first party and
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ as the second. The \emph{symmetric
	equivalents} of a bipartite relation of the form
	$M_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_\delta N_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$
	are the three relations
	\[
		N_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_\delta M_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,\qquad
		M_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'} \approx_\delta N_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''}\,,\qquad
		N_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'} \approx_\delta M_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''}\,,
	\]
	obtained by passing to the second bipartitioning scheme and by
	interchanging the first and second party; the symmetric equivalents of
	a single-party relation of the form
	$M_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx N_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}$ are the
	same relation on the register pairs $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$,
	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ and $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer to symmetric equivalents]
	\label{lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer}
	\notready
	\uses{def:symmetric-equivalents, def:expanded-state, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:symmetric-game, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
	Let $\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ be the projective strategy under
	analysis (Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention
	following it), assumed symmetric in the sense of
	Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-game}: the state $\ket{\psi}$ is
	invariant under exchanging registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$, and
	both players measure the same operators. Let $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ be the
	expanded state~\eqref{eq:def-psihat}, let
	\[
		\sigma \colon\;
		\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B},\quad
		\mathsf{A}' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}',\quad
		\mathsf{A}'' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}''\,,
		\qquad\qquad
		\theta \colon\;
		\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B},\quad
		\mathsf{A}' \leftrightarrow \mathsf{A}''\,,
	\]
	be the two permutations of the six registers
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''$
	given by these transpositions, and let $U_\sigma$ and $U_\theta$ be the
	corresponding permutation unitaries. Write
	$\Pi = \{\Id,\, U_\sigma,\, U_\theta,\, U_\sigma U_\theta\}$ and let
	\[
		\mathcal{R} = \{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}',\; \mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}'',\;
		\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}',\; \mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''\}
	\]
	be the four register placements of
	Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}. Then:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Every $U \in \Pi$ fixes $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and the induced
		action of $\Pi$ on $\mathcal{R}$ is simply transitive.
		\item Let $P$ and $Q$ be operators on
		$\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$, where $\hilb$ is the common Hilbert
		space of registers $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$, let
		$\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}', \mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' \in \mathcal{R}$ and
		let $U \in \Pi$. Then
		\[
			\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
			\,=\,
			\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} - (Q)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|\,,
		\]
		the placement notation being that of
		Definition~\ref{def:expanded-observables}. Consequently, for
		families $\{P^x_a\}$ and $\{Q^x_a\}$ indexed by a question $x$ drawn
		from a distribution and an answer $a$, and for every $\delta \ge 0$,
		$(P^x_a)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} \approx_\delta (Q^x_a)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'}$
		holds on $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ if and only if
		$(P^x_a)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} \approx_\delta (Q^x_a)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')}$
		does, with the same $\delta$
		(Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}).
	\end{enumerate}
	In particular, taking $\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}' = \mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$
	and $\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' = \mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$, respectively
	$\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}' = \mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, the images under
	$U_\theta$, $U_\sigma$ and $U_\sigma U_\theta$ are exactly the three
	symmetric equivalents of Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents},
	with the same error parameter.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:expanded-state, def:EPR, def:symmetric-game, def:povm-distance}
	Each of $\sigma$ and $\theta$ transposes registers carrying isomorphic
	Hilbert spaces --- $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$ both carry $\hilb$,
	and the four ancilla registers are all isomorphic to
	$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$ (Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state}) --- so the
	permutation unitaries $U_\sigma$ and $U_\theta$ are defined and satisfy
	$U (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} U^\dagger = (P)_{U(\mathsf{C})U(\mathsf{C}')}$
	for every operator $P$ and every placement.

	For item~1, both generators fix $\ket{\hat{\psi}} = (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}$:
	the factor $(\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}$ is invariant under
	$\mathsf{A} \leftrightarrow \mathsf{B}$ by the symmetry hypothesis;
	$\sigma$ exchanges the two ancilla factors, which are identical; and
	$\theta$ leaves $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}$
	untouched and exchanges the two halves of each pair in
	$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}$, under which
	$\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ is invariant (Definition~\ref{def:EPR}). The
	action on $\mathcal{R}$ sends $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$ to
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'$, $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$,
	$\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$ and $\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ under $\Id$,
	$U_\sigma$, $U_\theta$ and $U_\sigma U_\theta$ respectively, so it is
	simply transitive on the four placements.

	For item~2, insert $U^\dagger U$ and use $U \ket{\hat{\psi}} = \ket{\hat{\psi}}$
	together with unitary invariance of the norm:
	\[
		\bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
		= \bigl\| U \bigl( (P)_{\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}'} - (Q)_{\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}'} \bigr) U^\dagger \, U \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|
		= \bigl\| \bigl( (P)_{U(\mathsf{C}\mathsf{C}')} - (Q)_{U(\mathsf{D}\mathsf{D}')} \bigr) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \bigr\|\,.
	\]
	Summing the squares over the answers $a$ and averaging over the
	questions $x$ preserves the identity, so the two sides of the asserted
	equivalence of $\approx_\delta$ relations
	(Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) are equal quantities. The final
	assertion is item~1 applied to the placements listed there.
\end{proof}

5:# Overlap of expanded line and expanded point measurements
6:
7:This module computes the diagonal overlap, on the expanded state, between an
8:expanded line measurement on one placement and the expanded point effects
9:selected by evaluation at the sampled point on the opposite placement. Each
10:product of convolution terms factorizes into a strategy overlap and an EPR
11:overlap; the EPR overlap of a Pauli line projector with a Pauli point projector
12:vanishes unless the line polynomial evaluates to the point value, and then
13:equals the EPR overlap of the line projector alone. Summing over the
14:convolution fibers identifies the expanded overlap with the overlap of the
15:strategy's evaluation classes and its completed point measurement. This is the
16:computation displayed in items 2 and 3 of the expanded-line consistency lemma.

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Sandwich.Defs
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Conditional collision bounds from fiber averages
     5	
     6	This module converts an unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question
     7	fiber into the positive-mass conditional collision predicate used by the
     8	pasting theorem.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The conditional collision hypothesis is from `lem:pasting`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. Its use in
    14	the QPBT combining argument occurs at
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	/-- An unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question fiber implies
    27	the positive-mass conditional collision predicate of `lem:pasting`. This is a
    28	formalization-only normalization adapter for paper lines 504--525. -/
    29	theorem collision_bound_of_fiber_averages {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}
    30	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
    31	    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
    32	    [Fintype Γ₂] (dist : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂))
    33	    (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂) (eta : ℝ)
    34	    (hbound : ∀ fixed : X × Y₁, ∀ first second : Γ₂, first ≠ second →
    35	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then
    36	        (if eval₂ first sample.2 = eval₂ second sample.2 then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    37	      eta * avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then 1 else 0)) :
    38	    HasConditionalCollisionBound dist eval₂ eta := by
    39	  classical
    40	  intro question point _ first second hne
    41	  have havg (value : ((X × Y₁) × Y₂) → ℝ) :
    42	      avgOver dist value = ∑ sample, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
    43	    exact (dist.sum_univ_eq_sum_support _ (fun sample hout => by
    44	      rw [dist.outsideSupport sample hout, zero_mul])).symm
    45	  have hmass : (dist.map Prod.fst).weight (question, point) =
    46	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = (question, point) then 1 else 0) := by
    47	    rw [Distribution.map_weight]
    48	    unfold avgOver
    49	    rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    50	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    51	    intro sample _
    52	    by_cases hfixed : sample.1 = (question, point) <;> simp [hfixed]
    53	  rw [hmass]
    54	  have h := hbound (question, point) first second hne
    55	  simpa [havg, Fintype.sum_prod_type, mul_ite] using h
    56	
    57	end
    58	
    59	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
